newsitem.title: UK: Scottish tax power excludes savings, div income.
newsitem.headline: Scottish tax power excludes savings, div income.

text.p: The proposed Scottish parliament's power to vary income tax by as much as three pence in the pound will not extend to income from savings and dividends, the government said on Thursday.

Unveiling its plans for the first Scottish parliament for almost 300 years, the government said it wanted to ensure such income was taxed on a consistent basis throughout the United Kingdom in order to avoid economic distortions.

The Edinburgh parliament, which is expected to assume its full powers in January 2000, will be able to authorise the new Scottish Executive to undertake short-term borrowing to match income and expenditure.
"But it will not have a long-term borrowing power on its own account," the government's policy white paper said.
The ability to vary the basic rate of UK income tax by three pence in the pound currently represents about 450 million pounds.
To prevent future changes to UK income tax eroding the Scottish parliament's potential tax take, it will be guaranteed the right to 450 million pounds.
Furthermore, this tax-varying sum will be indexed to preserve its real value.

The details of how to protect Scotland's tax take would obviously depend on changes to the structure of the income tax system and would be a matter for discussion between the Scottish Executive and the UK government, the white paper said.
Anyone whose principal home is in Scotland or who spends half his time in Scotland (when in the UK) will be liable to Scottish tax.
The Inland Revenue will collect any tax due to the Scottish parliament.
The direct costs to the government of establishing the mechanisms for tax variation in Scotland is estimated at 10 million pounds, with annual running costs of eight million.
Setting-up costs for employers are estimated at 50 million pounds, with annual running costs of six million to 15 million pounds.
A small firm with five Scottish resident employees would typically face setting-up costs of 50-100 pounds, the government estimated. -- London newsroom 44-171-542 7767
